answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can trade, and checks that deposit on every pulse of activity. A gale of fake signups cannot reuse the same locked funds: each branch of the identity vine needs its own deposit. Running 10,000 active identities therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing a capital cost even though the attacker can eventually reclaim the money.
